name: Iowa
phones_sentence: County veterans affairs phones and addresses come from each office’s page on the Iowa Department of Veterans Affairs website. Hours are not listed there; call ahead.

offices.note: County Veteran Service Officers are accredited and help with VA claims, pension and survivor benefits at no charge.
offices.selection: Office address and phone as printed on each county office’s page on the department’s website, each read in full; officers’ names and emails omitted. The pages list no hours. aging.source_title: Iowa HHS: SFY 2025 Area Agency on Aging Plan Update Synopsis (Iowa Commission on Aging, June 10, 2025)
aging.source_scope: Each Area Agency on Aging’s counties, toll-free phone and offices; read in full. Prepared for the Iowa Commission on Aging meeting of June 10, 2025. LifeLong Links, 866-468-7887, connects callers to the right Area Agency on Aging (Iowa Attorney General, https://www.iowaattorneygeneral.gov/for-consumers/for-older-iowans/report-prevent-elder-abuse; search excerpt).
aging.description: Iowa’s six Area Agencies on Aging help adults 60 and older, people with disabilities and caregivers find help at home, meals, caregiver support, elder abuse prevention and options counseling.
aging.next_step_extra: LifeLong Links, 866-468-7887, also connects callers to their Area Agency on Aging.

programs.name: Iowa veterans: County Veteran Service Officers for claims help
programs.description: Free help with VA claims, appeals, pension and survivor benefits from the accredited County Veteran Service Officer in each of Iowa’s 99 county veterans affairs offices. County commissions of veteran affairs may also offer local emergency help. The Iowa Department of Veterans Affairs runs the Iowa Veterans Benefits Office at Camp Dodge.
programs.next_step: Choose a county above for its veterans affairs office. Or call the Iowa Department of Veterans Affairs at 515-252-4698 or 800-838-4692.
constraints: Many rural offices keep limited hours; call ahead.

programs.name: LifeLong Links and Iowa’s Area Agencies on Aging
programs.organization: Iowa Department of Health and Human Services and the six Area Agencies on Aging
programs.description: LifeLong Links is Iowa’s statewide aging and disability resource line; it connects older adults, people with disabilities and caregivers to their local Area Agency on Aging and long-term services. Military service is not required.
programs.next_step: Call LifeLong Links at 866-468-7887, or choose a county above for its Area Agency on Aging.
constraints: Each program has its own eligibility and waitlist.

programs.name: Medicare counseling (SHIIP) for Iowa
programs.organization: Iowa Insurance Division, Senior Health Insurance Information Program (SHIIP)
programs.description: Free, unbiased Medicare counseling from Iowa’s State Health Insurance Assistance Program, SHIIP, with trained volunteer counselors at local sites.
programs.next_step: Call SHIIP at 800-351-4664 (TTY 800-735-2942) to reach a counselor near you. For Medicare itself, call 800-MEDICARE (800-633-4227).
constraints: Counselor availability is limited during open enrollment; call early.

programs.name: Iowa Long-Term Care Ombudsman and dependent adult abuse reporting
programs.organization: Iowa HHS: Office of the State Long-Term Care Ombudsman; Dependent Adult Abuse Program
programs.description: Free, confidential advocacy for people living in nursing facilities, assisted living, residential care and elder group homes. Iowa HHS takes reports of abuse, neglect or exploitation of dependent adults living in the community, 24 hours a day.
programs.next_step: Call the ombudsman at 866-236-1430. To report dependent adult abuse in the community, call 800-362-2178 (24/7). For abuse in a licensed facility, call the Department of Inspections, Appeals and Licensing at 877-686-0027. In an emergency, call 911.
constraints: The ombudsman acts with the resident’s permission and is not a licensing agency.

programs.name: Free legal help for older Iowans
programs.organization: Iowa Legal Aid, Legal Hotline for Older Iowans
programs.description: The Legal Hotline for Older Iowans gives free civil legal help to Iowans 60 and older. Iowa Legal Aid helps low-income Iowans of any age.
programs.next_step: Age 60 and older: call the Legal Hotline for Older Iowans at 800-992-8161 (515-282-8161 in Des Moines). Under 60: Iowa Legal Aid, 800-532-1503.
constraints: The hotline handles civil matters only.

programs.name: VA health care systems serving Iowa
programs.description: Iowa veterans are served by the VA Central Iowa Health Care System (Des Moines VA Medical Center, 3600 30th Street; 515-699-5999, toll-free 800-294-8387) and the Iowa City VA Health Care System (601 Highway 6 West; 319-338-0581, toll-free 800-637-0128). Some western and northwestern counties are closer to VA systems in Omaha and Sioux Falls.
programs.next_step: Call the system nearest you, or use VA’s facility locator with your ZIP code. Not enrolled yet? Ask your county veterans affairs office for help applying.
constraints: Which system serves you depends on where you live; VA’s locator shows the right clinic.

coverage_scope: Referral edition. All 99 counties show their county veterans affairs office, their Area Agency on Aging and the statewide long-term care ombudsman; 29 counties also show a Center for Independent Living. The national directory lists no center for the other 70.
coverage_note: County veterans affairs offices come from the Iowa Department of Veterans Affairs county pages. Area Agencies on Aging come from the state’s SFY 2025 Area Plan synopsis. Independent living centers come from the ILRU national directory. Reviewed November 16, 2026. Contacts are not telephone-confirmed.
